why: The quiet half of the same rule as 24: the indices ascend, they simply skip one. `ToolCallFragment.index` is the call's position in the assistant turn, so 0 followed by 2 says there is a call at position 1 that this stream never mentioned — either the model made three calls and one was dropped in transit, or the provider's index is not a position at all. Neither can be resolved by guessing, and the second is the one that matters: the Anthropic grammar maps its block index onto this position, so admitting a sparse index here would make the same turn arrive with different canonical indices depending on which provider answered.
